solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In writing on death I tremble, making short notes

indicators.note: 'in' places the trembling self inside the letters standing for a piece of writing
in an across clue 'on' means set after, so the writing follows the death

blocks.note: demise is a formal word for death
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written
to quaver is to shake or tremble

explanation.surface: Someone shaking while writing about death, jotting brief notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short notes' reads as jottings, but it is musical: a demisemiquaver is a thirty-second note. 'In' puts the trembling self inside the writing, and 'on' sets that after death.
explanation.definitionFit: A demisemiquaver is a very brief musical note, half a semiquaver in length, so plural it means short notes.

clue.text: Winding stick first to break bulb

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is lodged within the other

blocks.note: daff is a short form of daffodil, which grows from a bulb
first is written 1ST, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A winding stick breaks first into a flower bulb in some garden mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: First as 1ST, with the digit read as a letter, is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A distaff is the rod on which wool or flax is wound before spinning, a stick used for winding.

clue.text: Scrum half came over the protected side

indicators.note: only half of the word that follows is kept, here its second pair of letters

blocks.note: the back half of the word came
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A rugby scrum-half comes round to the sheltered side of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrum half' reads as one rugby position; split it and Scrum is the definition. In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused, disorderly scuffle of people, just like a scrum in its looser sense of a crush.

clue.text: Stop house officer discharging the last two

indicators.note: discharging means letting go, so the final two letters are dropped from the officer

blocks.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
a colonel is an army officer

explanation.surface: A house officer, a junior hospital doctor, stops discharging the last two patients.
explanation.walkthrough: House officer is a junior hospital doctor in Britain, but here house and officer are separate pieces. A semi is a house joined to its neighbour on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicolon is a punctuation mark, and stop is an old general term for a punctuation mark.

clue.text: State one’s lost a lot of hair

indicators.note: one is the letter I, and being lost means it leaves the word

blocks.note: Maine is a US state
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A US state reports that someone has lost a great deal of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A mane is a thick mass of hair, on a horse or lion or a person with abundant locks.

clue.text: Some verse as a sequence

blocks.note: qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
a train of thought or events is a sequence

explanation.surface: A bit of poetry presented as a sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: Qua, meaning 'in the role of', is used in English: 'art qua art'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quatrain is a stanza of four lines, so it is a portion of verse.

clue.text: Rifle at first a boy keeps firing wickedly

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word just before is wanted
to keep something is to hold it within, so the boy's letters surround the other

blocks.note: a boy is a son
the initial letter of rifle

explanation.surface: A boy hangs on to a rifle, shooting maliciously.
explanation.walkthrough: Firing suggests guns after rifle, but here it means setting fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting property alight, so it is malicious firing.

clue.text: Enthusiastic blue exercising, right on time

indicators.note: exercising letters means moving them about and working them into a new order
in a down clue 'on' stacks one piece above the next

blocks.note: the letters of blue rearranged
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone feeling blue cheers up by exercising and arriving punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' wants to be R, but it is the legal right called a lien.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling with energy and cheer, which is a synonym for enthusiastic.

clue.text: Pair of creatures, big and small, that makes a bond

blocks.note: a seal is the big creature of the pair
an ant is the small creature

explanation.surface: Two animals, one large and one tiny, form a bond of friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair of creatures' says two animals are needed; big and small tell you which size each is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a substance applied to close joints, sticking surfaces together so it forms a bond.

clue.text: City proposal a man casually trimmed

indicators.note: trimming cuts away the outer letters of the phrase, leaving the run inside

blocks.note: the letters run across these words once their outer parts are trimmed

explanation.surface: A man makes a casual, cut-short proposal in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts with the last three letters of proposal and ends with the first two of casually.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamanca is a historic university city in western Spain, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Endlessly sad, relative not quite fitting in sweater

indicators.note: without its end the word loses its final letter
not quite all of the relative is used, so its last letter goes
fitting in means slotting inside the other piece

blocks.note: sad with its last letter cut
an aunt is a relative, here missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A miserable relative's jumper doesn't quite fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweater reads as a jumper (a British word for a knitted pullover), but it is a place that makes you sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a hot room for sweating, so whimsically it is a sweater, something that makes people perspire.

clue.text: A kitchen only half finished leads to comment

indicators.note: work only half finished stops at the midpoint, so just the first half survives

blocks.note: taken as written
the kitchen is orchestral slang for the percussion section

explanation.surface: An unfinished kitchen refit prompts a remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen is musicians' slang for the percussion section, with its pots-and-pans array of instruments; keep the first five of its ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief insightful remark or observation, so a comment.

clue.text: Silk cut completely the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards, so that word is read from its end

blocks.note: to prune is to cut back
all means wholly, completely

explanation.surface: A cheap silk was cut entirely wrongly by the tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a strong twilled fabric, formerly of silk or worsted, used for gowns and shoe uppers.

clue.text: After start of fire close damaged platform

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled
after places the jumbled word behind the single letter

blocks.note: the first letter of fire
the letters of close rearranged

explanation.surface: After a fire broke out, a nearby platform was damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Fo'c'sle is the sailor's contraction of forecastle, its apostrophes dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The fo'c'sle is the raised deck at a ship's bow, a platform at the front of the vessel.

clue.text: Endless street party getting noisier

indicators.note: with no end the word drops its final letter

blocks.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A never-ending street party gets louder and louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Crescendo is the musical term for a gradual increase in volume, so a passage growing louder.

clue.text: Most active local objector finally failing in case

indicators.note: failing at the end means the last letter drops away

blocks.note: a nimby objects to developments in their own area: not in my back yard
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A local protester's objection eventually fails in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a container signal, but it is the word lest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimblest is the superlative of nimble, meaning quickest and most agile, so most active.

clue.text: One prepared to compromise who wins a second medal?

blocks.note: first meaning: a haggler who will meet halfway
second meaning, split into two words: a second award of a medal is marked by a clasp added to its ribbon, so the winner is a gainer of that clasp

explanation.walkthrough: Split BAR GAINER: a bar is the clasp added to a medal ribbon when the honour is awarded again. The question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargainer haggles over terms and will settle for a middle price, so is ready to compromise.

clue.text: Simple house deceptively described

blocks.note: a home is a house
a story spun is one given a misleading slant

explanation.surface: An estate agent misleadingly describes a plain house.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, like cloth woven at home, so simple.

clue.text: African native, singular youth, getting nothing out of paperback

indicators.note: taking nothing out means removing the round letter that looks like zero

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a teen is a youth
nothing is zero, the letter O
a paperback is a book

explanation.surface: A unique young African gets nothing from reading a paperback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African native' suggests a person, but it is an animal native to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The steenbok is a small antelope of southern and eastern Africa, so an animal native to that continent.

clue.text: Welcoming opening of restaurant, rank heavenly spread

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: status is rank or standing
the first letter of restaurant

explanation.surface: A smart restaurant welcomes guests to a lavish, heavenly buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' suggests a feast after restaurant, but it is a layer spread across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, flat cloud forming a uniform grey sheet, a layer spread across the heavens.

clue.text: Squirm and shrivel when right out of place

indicators.note: the right-hand letter R is put out of place, so only that one letter moves within the word

blocks.note: to wither is to shrivel

explanation.surface: Someone squirms and shrinks when their right is challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' names the one letter that moves: shift the R from fifth place to second.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about in pain or discomfort, so to squirm.

clue.text: Sheep wandering over American city, wonderful old place

indicators.note: wandering things stray about, so the letters roam into a new order
in a down clue over places the jumbled word above the next piece

blocks.note: the letters of sheep rearranged
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Sheep roam over an American town, a marvellous spot of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonderful' is literal: Ephesus had the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus is an ancient Greek city in modern Turkey, home to one of the Seven Wonders.

clue.text: One replacing a string? Not on this instrument

blocks.note: first meaning, read in parts: someone who cords again, putting a new string on
second meaning: a woodwind instrument, which has no strings to replace

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as RE-CORDER: one who cords again. 'Not on this instrument' then jokes that the job never arises, since the instrument is blown, not strung.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a simple wooden or plastic wind instrument with finger holes, played by blowing.

clue.text: Sport a red frill

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, is a famous red

explanation.surface: Someone wears a red frilly decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a verb meaning wear; it is a noun, the game of rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered strip of fabric used as trimming, a frill on a dress or curtain.

clue.text: Passion and fight oddly saved match

indicators.note: only the letters in odd-numbered positions are saved, the rest discarded

blocks.note: a war is a fight
the first, third and fifth letters of match

explanation.surface: Fervour and a fighting spirit strangely rescued a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth means strong feeling or ardour, so it is a synonym for passion.

clue.text: Perform improperly with paste, hiding diamonds

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked away inside, so the paste wraps the other piece

blocks.note: miso is a Japanese paste of fermented soya beans
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A con artist works dishonestly with fake paste gems, concealing the real diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Paste is also imitation jewellery, which suits the diamonds; here it is the soy food.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdo is to do something wrongly or badly, so to carry it out improperly.

clue.text: Back of room, one in school?

indicators.note: 'back of' asks for the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to back something is to be for it
the back letter of room

explanation.surface: A pupil sits at the back of the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' does double work: it supplies FOR, as in backing a cause, and also says to take the back letter of room. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a class or year group in a British school, one of several in a school.

clue.text: Stomach mostly visible with shortened attractive garment

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter is cut
a shortened word is clipped at its end

blocks.note: tum is a childish word for stomach
nice means pleasing or attractive

explanation.surface: A cropped, alluring top leaves most of the belly on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose sleeveless garment reaching to the hips or knees, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Outlook for love: signs are mixed

indicators.note: mixed things are stirred together, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horoscope's love forecast is muddled, since the signs disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: The O for love joins signs before the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast of how things will turn out, a likely outlook.

clue.text: Misleading items in papers on French author taking in ass

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the author's name wraps the animal
in an across clue 'on' places the papers after the author

blocks.note: George Sand was a French novelist
moke is British slang for a donkey
the Mirror is a British newspaper, so mirrors are papers

explanation.surface: Deceptive stories in newspapers about a French writer who fooled an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ass reads as a fool but is the animal; moke is an old British word for a donkey. The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke and mirrors are illusionists' props, so the phrase means deceptive tricks designed to mislead.
